I have farmed these 16 mu in Quzhou County for 35 years. I am 65 now, and I know every piece of this land. I only finished primary school, but I learned farming from my father and from watching what works. I don't need books to tell me what my own eyes can see.

My farm is 16.1 mu. I keep about 10 mu in wheat-maize rotation—that is my bread and butter. I have 4 mu of garlic because garlic brings good money if the price holds. The remaining 2.1 mu is cotton. I have my own well, so I can irrigate when I need to. There are five mouths to feed in my house.

Right now it is autumn. I just cut the maize and I am preparing to plant winter wheat and garlic. I hire Old Zhang's rotary tiller for 30 yuan per mu. I buy improved wheat seed from the dealer in town—the kind most people around here plant. I use 25 jin of seed per mu.

For the 10 mu of wheat, I put down one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu when I plant. That is the kind with 15-15-15 printed on the bag. Then in spring, when the wheat turns green after winter, I spread urea twice. The first time at green-up, I put 50 jin per mu. The second time at jointing, I put another 25 jin per mu. I also spray for weeds once and for aphids once. I irrigate three times: after planting if it is dry, then at green-up in March, then at grain filling in May.

For the maize I will plant next June after cutting the wheat, I use hybrid seed—about 3 jin per mu. I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time. Then I side-dress urea twice: 30 jin per mu when the plants are knee-high, and 20 jin per mu when they are shooting tassels. I irrigate twice, three times if July is very hot and dry. I spray for armyworm twice.

For my 4 mu of garlic, I plant it now in autumn using the big cloves I saved from my best harvest. Garlic needs soft ground, so I till it deep with the rotary. I put one and a half bags of compound fertilizer per mu—that is 75 jin. I also buy half a bag of potassium fertilizer per mu because garlic needs more potassium than wheat. In spring, when the garlic starts growing fast, I topdress with 50 jin of urea per mu, split into two times. I water garlic four times for sure. I spray fungicide three times because garlic can get rust.

For the 2.1 mu of cotton, I will plant it next spring. I use my own saved seed—the local kind, not hybrid. I plough the cotton field deep in spring. Cotton cannot have too much nitrogen or it grows too tall and the bolls drop. I use three-quarters of a bag of compound per mu—that is about 35 jin. Then I topdress with 20 jin of urea per mu twice. I irrigate three times and spray for bollworm three times.

I think about costs every day. A bag of compound costs about 160 yuan now, and urea is about 100 yuan. For my 10 mu of wheat, that is 10 bags of compound and 15 bags of urea. That is 2,600 yuan just for fertilizer. But I learned my lesson—two years ago my cousin tried to save money by using less fertilizer, and his wheat turned yellow and only gave 600 jin per mu. He lost thousands of yuan. I would rather spend an extra 500 yuan on fertilizer than risk losing a whole harvest.

I expect my wheat to yield about 900 jin per mu, the maize about 1,000 jin per mu, garlic about 2,400 jin per mu, and cotton about 560 jin of seed cotton per mu. If the weather is normal and no big disaster comes, these numbers are what I always get.
